subject: physics
title: Damping, Forced Oscillation and Resonance
welcome_lead: Add friction and a driver — and discover resonance peaks and bridge disasters.
meta_desc: A-Level SHM adventure on damping types, forced oscillation and resonance behaviour.
final_note: Lower damping means a sharper, taller resonance peak.

concepts.def: Energy loss reducing amplitude over time.

walkthroughs.body_html: Light: amplitude envelope decays exponentially. Heavy: slow return, no oscillation. Critical: fastest non-oscillating return — used in car suspensions.
A driver applies a periodic force at frequency f_d. The oscillator responds with a steady-state amplitude depending on f_d, natural frequency f_0 and damping.
When f_d = f_0, amplitude peaks. Less damping → sharper, taller peak. Examples: Tacoma Narrows bridge, microwave heating water at 2.45 GHz, MRI scanners.

mcqs.q: If an object is moving at constant velocity in a straight line, what is the net force on it?
options: The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.
There must be a forward force on the object to keep it moving.
Zero — by Newton's first law, constant velocity requires zero net force.
The car's own momentum acts as a force that drives it in a circle.

mcqs.q: For a projectile launched horizontally, what affects the horizontal component of velocity during flight (ignoring air resistance)?
options: The car's own momentum acts as a force that drives it in a circle.
Gravity slows down both the vertical and horizontal motion.
The horizontal velocity increases over time because the projectile is falling.
Nothing — horizontal velocity stays constant; only vertical velocity changes due to gravity.

mcqs.q: What force keeps a car moving in a circle around a bend?
options: The car's own momentum acts as a force that drives it in a circle.
Friction from the road acting towards the centre of the circle — centripetal force.
The horizontal velocity increases over time because the projectile is falling.
A centrifugal force pushes the car outwards from the centre.
